transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-05
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Sofia Martinez (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Lena Park (CTO, Mirage Commerce), Jordan Smith (Lead ML Eng), Carmen Ruiz (Infra)

Summary:
Quick Optimize walkthrough focused on batching and prefix/KV cache recommendations for Mirage Commerce's conversational product (product search + personalization). Delivered a savings sandbox simulation in the console, discussed tradeoffs between latency and unit cost, and agreed to a 2-week pilot benchmark.

Topics:
- Current stack & constraints (in-house g4 fleet, 80ms avg token gen, high variance on tail)
- Cost-sim scenarios (sessionization, batching windows, KV prefetching)
- Console Optimize walkthrough: batching profiles, cache TTL, quantization tiering
- Pilot scope and next steps (data share, benchmark script)

Action items (recap in call):
- See metadata action_items (below)

Transcript:
[00:00] Sofia (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll do a 45-ish minute walkthrough, then leave some time for Qs. I'm Sofia, AE on the account, joined by Ravi from our infra/optimize team.
[00:18] Ravi (Redwood): Hi all, hey, um, excited to look at Mirage's pattern. We got the notes from the intake form, thanks Lena.
[00:25] Lena (Mirage): Yeah thanks, and thanks for doing the sandbox, we're hoping to knock down our token spend.
[00:34] Jordan (Mirage): Quick note, our highest volume is product search chat, average prompt length about 120 tokens, response 60 tokens, but we have a long tail when people paste descriptions.
[00:46] Carmen (Mirage): Also, infra constraint: we can't move traffic out of eu-west-1 for regulatory reasons. We need VPC + bring-your-own-key KMS.
[00:58] Sofia (Redwood): Great, we'll keep that in mind — we have region routing and VPC deployment options. Ok Ravi, want to start the console demo?
[01:05] Ravi (Redwood): Yep. I'm sharing my screen — sorry, can everyone see the Optimize console? (pause) Looks good. First slide: baseline. We imported Mirage's 7-day sample trace you provided, and created three scenarios: conservative, balanced, aggressive.
[01:26] Ravi (Redwood): Baseline numbers — on your current profile (in-house g4-ish latency and no cache), cost per 1k requests is roughly $18 and median latency 110ms, with 95p tail up to 420ms. Those tails are where batching and prefix caching can help.
[01:47] Jordan (Mirage): Wait $18 per 1k? That seems higher than we expected — is that with token accounting?
[01:53] Ravi (Redwood): Yes, tokenized cost plus the per-inference GPU amortization. In the sandbox we model both token usage and infra time.
[02:02] Lena (Mirage): How much of that is from long responses versus many small sessions?
[02:08] Ravi (Redwood): Good question. The heatmap shows 60% of cost is in 10% of sessions — the long-tail sessions. The rest is steady-state. Prefetching KV cache for sessionized users and batching small requests into micro-batches reduces per-token GPU overhead.
[02:24] Sofia (Redwood): I'll also flag the option to route low-complexity prompts to a quantized small model variant — we used a mixed-tier model profile in the aggressive scenario.
[02:34] Jordan (Mirage): How safe is that for relevance? Our product search is sensitive.
[02:38] Ravi (Redwood): We instrumented quality gates: A/B evaluation on the top-10 results and automated regressions. In the sim we enforced a 0.5% quality regression budget. You can define that in the Console and we'll alert if a rollout violates it.
[02:52] [03:00] -- 3-minute mark, Laura? (misattributed) --
[03:04] Lena (Mirage): Can you show the batching profile? We tried a naive 100ms delay but saw tail latency spike.
[03:11] Ravi (Redwood): Yep. Here in Optimize -> Batching, we have continuous-batching settings and latency SLO targets. For Mirage's traffic shape we recommended a dynamic target: prefer low-latency windows for interactive sessions (<=30ms batch delay) and allow 80-120ms for background bulk tasks. The trick is session-affinity: keep a user's KV cache warm so longer batches don't re-generate context.
[03:37] Jordan (Mirage): Session-affinity — are we talking sticky routing? We don't want to pin to a single GPU forever.
[03:43] Ravi (Redwood): Not sticky forever — session affinity with soft ttl (e.g., 30m) and automatic rehydrate to a compatible host if evicted. Prefix/KV caching stores the prefix key and cached KV to avoid recompute on warm sessions.
[03:56] Carmen (Mirage): How does that affect memory footprint on the node? We're limited on GPU memory.
[04:02] Ravi (Redwood): We have two levers — KV cache TTL and prefetch window. Shorter TTL reduces memory but increases cold-call cost. We showed a memory vs cost curve; the balanced scenario used a TTL of 15 minutes and prefetch only for high-value sessions — top 20% by predicted LTV.
[04:20] Lena (Mirage): Predicted LTV tagging — useful. How do we mark those sessions?
[04:26] Sofia (Redwood): You can send an attribute in the request header (session_score) or use our Console rules to tag based on user_id behavior. This drives prefetch and priority routing.
[04:36] [05:00] Jordan (Mirage): There's also the question of dedicated vs hosted. We prefer hosted for simplicity but have strict audit controls.
[05:07] Sofia (Redwood): For Mirage, Hosted with VPC peering + customer-managed KMS would meet most needs. If you need on-prem, Redwood Private is possible but adds timeline. Hosted + VPC gives a middle ground.
[05:20] Carmen (Mirage): We need SOC 2 and a network diagram for the security review.
[05:25] Sofia (Redwood): Absolutely — I'll attach SOC2 report and the VPC/network diagram after this call.
[05:30] Ravi (Redwood): Back to the cost sim — the aggressive scenario used KV prefetch for top 20% sessions plus batching window 80ms and quantized model for low-complexity prompts. That scenario reduced unit cost by 37% but increased median latency to ~130ms. Balanced saved ~21% with median latency ~115ms and 95p tail 300ms.
[05:52] Jordan (Mirage): The tradeoff is clear. But what about tail spikes — how do you handle sudden traffic bursts?
[05:59] Ravi (Redwood): Smart routing and burst capacity. If a node hits CPU/GPU pressure we fallback to a compatible variant (smaller model or cross-region if allowed). We also surface autoscale buffers in the Console.
[06:12] [06:30] Lena (Mirage): Show the actual simulation spreadsheet please?
[06:34] Ravi (Redwood): Sure — link in chat: https://drive.google.com/sandbox-mirage-cost-sim (note: placeholder). The sheet enumerates scenarios with assumptions: token mix, sessionization rate, cache hit ratio, prefetch hit, batching gain factor.
[06:50] Jordan (Mirage): On caching hit ratio — how realistic is your assumed 45% hit for KV prefetch?
[06:56] Ravi (Redwood): That number came from your 7-day sample where repeated sessions had high overlap. But we can tune: prefetch policy, TTL, and similarity thresholds. If your prompts vary a lot, hit rate drops and prefetch might not be worth it.
[07:12] Lena (Mirage): We have enterprise customers that occasionally paste huge catalogs in the chat — those blow out context windows. Any recommendations?
[07:20] Ravi (Redwood): For very long prompts, we recommend a pipeline: on-device extraction -> indexed retrieval -> short prompt to the model. Also consider truncation policies and sentinel tokens. Those reduce average tokenization. In the sim we treated big uploads as background jobs and batched them.
[07:38] Sofia (Redwood): Also, you can set an opt-in prefetch for heavy users — only prefetch if they cross a threshold.
[07:45] [08:00] Jordan (Mirage): Security detail: KMS — can we bring our own key and have Redwood not see plaintext?
[08:06] Sofia (Redwood): Yes, BYOK supported in Private and Hosted with VPC+KMS integration. We can configure envelope encryption and limit plaintext view. We'll include the architecture doc.
[08:15] Carmen (Mirage): Great. Also timeline — we need results in Q4 for budget sign-off.
[08:20] Sofia (Redwood): That works — we proposed a 2-week pilot to validate the sim and collect telemetry. If successful, we'll convert to a reserved capacity or dedicated path.
[08:28] Ravi (Redwood): I'll dig into one of the more interesting pieces — the micro-batching math. Essentially: batching reduces per-request GPU kernel overhead; we model per-batch amortized cost as base_cost + per_token*tokens. The benefit depends on concurrency and arrival rate distributions.
[08:47] Jordan (Mirage): Do you assume synchronous or async client behavior? Our frontend uses a streaming websocket currently.
[08:53] Ravi (Redwood): We modeled streaming clients. Redwood's runtime supports partial responses and merge-attribution so streaming and batching can coexist. For streaming, we batch micro-chunks if latencies allow, otherwise send partials.
[09:08] [10:00] -- timestamp jump --
[10:05] Lena (Mirage): Can you show the Console's per-route cost breakdown?
[10:10] Ravi (Redwood): Yep — per-route tokens, per-model compute time, and cost per token columns. You can filter by user cohort, route, and time. Here's a neat view — cost delta if we flip the route to quantized-small.
[10:26] Jordan (Mirage): I'd like to see a safety/quality delta too.
[10:29] Ravi (Redwood): You can overlay eval metrics — we have a per-prompt eval harness and alerting. We keep the top-of-funnel QA in the loop.
[10:40] Carmen (Mirage): Who'd be responsible for the pilot infra? Does Mirage need to provision anything?
[10:44] Sofia (Redwood): Minimal from you — provide traffic sample and a short whitelist of test users. We can run the pilot in Hosted with your VPC. If you want fully isolated HW we'll talk Dedicated.
[10:58] Lena (Mirage): Ok that seems doable.
[11:02] [12:00] Ravi (Redwood): One more thing — prefix caching is super effective for chat-like sessions where the beginning of the conversation repeats. It stores KV pairs for prefix tokens so subsequent steps avoid recompute. Prefetch warms the KV when a user is predicted to continue.
[12:20] Jordan (Mirage): Any gotchas?
[12:23] Ravi (Redwood): Memory pressure and cold-start cost if TTL too short. Also, ensure eviction policies align with user LTV — evict low-value sessions first.
[12:33] Sofia (Redwood): Another operational tip: rollouts in Canary mode with autobump back to the previous model if evals drop.
[12:40] Lena (Mirage): And observability — do we get token-level cost?
[12:44] Ravi (Redwood): Yes, token-level and model-time breakdowns per-request. We'll forward a sample trace viewer link.
[12:52] [20:00] -- mid-call more detailed sim walkthrough --
[20:12] Ravi (Redwood): I'm stepping through the cost-sim table: baseline $18/1k, balanced $14.2/1k, aggressive $11.4/1k. The aggressive uses a 42% cache hit and 2.6x batching gain on small requests. Balanced assumes 25% hit and 1.7x batching.
[20:30] Jordan (Mirage): Those batching gain multipliers — how do you get them?
[20:33] Ravi (Redwood): From kernel-level profiling and our field telemetry; it's a combination of continuous batching efficiencies and reduced per-call kernel launches. We also use quantization to reduce kernel runtime.
[20:45] Lena (Mirage): Are there any legal considerations for moving to Redwood Hosted? Data residency?
[20:50] Sofia (Redwood): You can pin region to eu-west-1, and we support data retention controls. For higher compliance, Private deployment or dedicated tenancy are options.
[20:58] Carmen (Mirage): Ok good.
[21:05] [30:00] -- late call Q&A and objections --
[30:10] Jordan (Mirage): What's the SLA guarantee on latency? We need stable p95 in contract.
[30:15] Sofia (Redwood): For Dedicated we offer tighter SLOs and contractual SLAs; Hosted has SLOs with credits for breaches. We'll include the SLA matrix.
[30:25] Jordan (Mirage): If we go dedicated, can we still use the console optimize features?
[30:29] Ravi (Redwood): Yes, same console — rollout, batching profiles, and the cost sim are available; some metrics' retention depends on the plan.
[30:38] Lena (Mirage): One more: pricing model — usage vs reserved.
[30:42] Sofia (Redwood): Hosted is usage-based; Dedicated adds a commit for reserved capacity with lower per-unit costs. We'll model both in the sim.
[30:50] [40:00] -- wrap up --
[40:05] Sofia (Redwood): Ok, recap: we'll send the annotated cost-sim, SOC2 and VPC diagram, and propose pilot dates. Ravi will run the extra throughput sim. Lena to provide traffic CSV and prompt set.
[40:20] Lena (Mirage): Sounds good. Can we get the spreadsheet with scenario assumptions inline so our finance team can review?
[40:26] Sofia (Redwood): Yep I'll add an assumptions tab and a short note explaining each variable.
[40:32] Jordan (Mirage): Also please include a sample benchmarking script; we want to mirror it on our side.
[40:36] Ravi (Redwood): I'll attach the benchmark harness and a README.
[40:41] Carmen (Mirage): Logistics: who schedules the pilot kickoff?
[40:44] Sofia (Redwood): I'll schedule it once we get the traffic CSV and confirm dates — propose 2026-10-18 start.
[40:52] [50:00] -- final clarifications --
[50:05] Lena (Mirage): One final ask — can you show an example of how the prefix cache looks in logs? We want to see cache hits in our SIEM.
[50:13] Ravi (Redwood): Yep, there's a log sample — it shows prefix_key, hit/miss, model_variant. I'll include a redacted example.
[50:25] Sofia (Redwood): Thanks everyone — we'll follow up.
[50:30] Jordan (Mirage): Thanks, this was helpful.
[50:33] Lena (Mirage): Thank you.
[50:35] Carmen (Mirage): Bye.

End of transcript.
